## Result

- Skill: proposal-review
- Review status: approved
- Vision alignment: aligned
- Material findings: none
- Open blockers: none
- Proposal readiness: direction and embedded feasibility are sufficient for authorized Design authoring; current governing authority remains in force until reviewed adoption.
- Immediate next stage: isolated stop before Design.
- Automatic downstream handoff: none.
- Claim limitations: approval covers direction, bounds and feasibility only. It does not approve exact model inventory, compatibility policy, source deletions, governing amendments, implementation, proof adequacy, release, publication or customer adoption.

## Review Dimensions

- Challenge: pass. The overlap is observable in both authored skills: each explicitly assigns living-model authorship while ordinary roles and handoffs retain specification/architecture separation. The system architecture combines current ownership amendments with historical descriptions. The proposal explains why a rename would leave engineering ownership unresolved.
- Goals: pass. Unified authoring, composed-system understanding, behavior/feasibility reconciliation, representative acceptance and a bounded demonstrator are outcome-oriented and preserve independent assessment.
- Scope: pass. The responsibility-based first slice is bounded to design authoring/model composition and directly affected consumers. Design must select exact clauses, decisions, subjects and consumers before Delivery. Full repository consolidation is explicitly deferred with maintainer direction ownership, Route assignment and durable follow-up required before closeout.
- Governing principle: pass. One current owner per engineering obligation/shared interaction and an explicit assessment basis is concise and implementation-independent.
- Direction: pass. The normal design path reconciles behavior, technical realization, decisions and acceptance under coherent model ownership; composition references local owners without creating a governance override. Installed guidance and old invocation compatibility are coordinated dependencies.
- Feasibility: pass. Exactly one embedded assessment relies on existing living-model instructions, Workflow WF-SR-07/08 and Responsibility-specific updates, and existing architecture/Test methods. It exposes compatibility, mixed-source ownership, decision preservation and public guidance constraints. No direction-level blocker is evidenced; exhaustive membership and exact amendments properly remain Design work.
- Material impact: pass. Conditional loading, oversized system views, coexistence and invocation compatibility are disclosed. The Constitution's separate-authorship/fixed-package review rules are explicitly included in the amendment direction, with no immediate override or premature adoption.
- Vision alignment: pass; aligned. The direction strengthens inspectable requirements, design rationale, proof derivation and durable ownership while retaining human direction, independent review and external-action boundaries. Changing artifact packaging does not abandon the vision's traceability chain.
- Downstream authority: pass. Exact inventories, deletions and compatibility mechanics remain Design; concrete checks, commands, milestones and integrated proof allocation remain Delivery; fixtures/assertions and actual results remain their existing owners. Representative scenarios neither restrict legitimate tests nor transfer Test or Review and Closeout policy ownership.
- Requested decision: pass. Approval selects a unified authoring capability and the first bounded consolidation, including the direction of necessary governing amendments. It expressly excludes final design, implementation, runtime schema change and separately authorized external actions.

## Scope Preservation Review

- Scope-preservation result: pass. Compared the complete proposal against the supplied original direction. All six requested outcome families remain visible: unified design skill; model-centered engineering; system/component cooperation; assessment and test derivation; first migration; and deferred remaining consolidation. Added governance/consumer coordination makes an existing dependency explicit. The scope table distinguishes core work, same-slice dependencies, the included migration slice, deferred work and excluded release/adoption. The deferral names its direction owner, routing owner and durable-assignment obligation; it does not claim later changes are executed or approved.

## Recommended Proposal Edits

- Recommended edits: none required. The Feasibility paragraph about an isolated authoring invocation is understood as provenance of that earlier invocation. This review uses the subsequently established exact change context; it does not rely on failed repository-wide discovery or infer absence of other governed work.

## Recommendation

- Recommendation: approved. The selected direction is valuable, credible and bounded enough for responsible Design. Preserve the declared governance reconciliation, exact first-slice inventory, public invocation transition and retained-owner/follow-up mapping as Design obligations. This review does not select or execute the next activity.

## Specialized-gate group

- Active gate predicates: scope_budget_context.
- Gate outcomes: pass. Public authoring, consumer alignment, governance and migration are classified; deferred consolidation has explicit follow-up ownership. vision_exception_context and standing_artifact_context are false: VISION.md and CONSTITUTION.md exist, the direction aligns with the vision, and no bootstrap exception is requested.
- Trigger ambiguity: none.
- Assembly: PRR1G-recorded-context-gated.
- Modes: formal-lifecycle/manual.

## Durable-recording group

- Recording status: recorded.
- Recording blocker: none.
- Record path: docs/changes/2026-09-08-unified-design-authoring-and-bounded-model-consolidation/reviews/proposal-review.json
- Finding-record paths: none.

## Formal-review group

- Review ID: proposal-review.
- Review record: docs/changes/2026-09-08-unified-design-authoring-and-bounded-model-consolidation/reviews/proposal-review.json
- Governed change identity: 2026-09-08-unified-design-authoring-and-bounded-model-consolidation
- Independence provenance: separate reviewer agent task /root/independent_proposal_review was assigned after the proposal was authored and the user explicitly authorized delegation. Contributors are user (original direction) and primary-agent (proposal author). This reviewer authored no part of the proposal, made no corrections to it, and independently inspected the complete subject and its cited decision basis. Independence derives from this concrete contributor separation, not the stored reviewer label.
- Assessment scope: the complete proposal at the exact subject identity stored in this review. Cited source excerpts support direction-level claims; this is not approval of every clause or historical authority in those source files.
- Evidence selection: original user direction; complete proposal, Constitution and vision; cited authored skills and architecture/Test resources; Workflow model ownership/document/proof sections; system architecture ownership amendments and architecture-method contract; Test and Review and Closeout ownership/assessment requirements. No project-map reliance: the proposal declares the older map unsuitable for current ownership. CLI source inspection was limited to recovering the valid context-selector envelope after an invalid selector, not used to infer semantic readiness. Scoped context selects proposal, activity, review, finding, blocker and applicability at full detail and reports a complete selection with no pre-existing reviews/findings/blockers. Subject inspection captured the exact basis identities below.
